A bicycle can stay upright because it has two wheels that rotate in opposite directions and have friction with the ground. When you pedal, the front wheel turns counterclockwise while the back wheel turns clockwise. This creates a torque that keeps the bike moving forward.

2. Set specific goals: Clearly defining what you want to achieve during the meeting can help focus the discussion and prevent unnecessary tangents.

3. Prioritize topics: Not all topics in a meeting need equal attention. By prioritizing which topics will have the most impact or benefit, you can streamline the meeting process.

4. Encourage participation: Make sure every participant has a chance to speak and contribute their ideas. This can help generate more value from the meeting and reduce its length.
